faq.question: Do you take insurance?
faq.answer: No — Cultivate Counseling Ohio is private-pay only. For many clients this is a feature, not a drawback: nothing is billed to insurance, so no diagnosis is filed on your permanent medical record, and what we work on stays entirely between us.

faq.question: What does a session cost?
faq.answer: See the fee listed above. Under the federal No Surprises Act, you have the right to receive a good-faith estimate of the expected cost of your care before you begin — just ask.

faq.question: What happens in a first session?
faq.answer: The first session is a conversation, not an interrogation. You share what you're comfortable sharing, Matthew explains how he works, and together you decide whether it feels like a fit. There is no obligation to continue.

faq.question: Do I have to talk about faith?
faq.answer: No. Faith-based integration is available if — and only if — you want it. It is never assumed, and choosing not to include it changes nothing about your care.

faq.question: Can we meet online?
faq.answer: Yes. Sessions are available in person at the West Chester office or by secure telehealth. Matthew is licensed in Ohio, so telehealth clients must be located in Ohio.

faq.question: Is what I say confidential?
faq.answer: Yes, within the limits the law requires of every licensed counselor (such as imminent risk of harm). Those limits are explained clearly before your first session.
